Some features require a subscription, with Spark limited to Google AI Pro and higher, while Daily Brief requires Google AI Plus or higher. When Gemini Live was first introduced back in 2024, its distinction from the regular Gemini experience was clear. Gemini would handle complex text-based queries, while Live would be the conversational assistant for free-flowing conversations. Although that distinction remains for the most part, Google is giving Gemini Live a much bigger role in getting things done, which might just be the gateway to blurring the lines in the future. According to Google, 63% of Gemini users talk to the assistant out loud. That stat was seemingly enough to convince the tech giant that Gemini Live shouldn’t just be a way to chat with Gemini. title: Building Foresight for Earth Science, featuring Lindsey Jacobson
summary: NASA’s Earth-observing satellite missions track dozens of features of a changing planet — aerosols, sea levels, land cover, cloud cover — over years and decades. Sustaining that record for the scientific and operational communities who depend on it requires more than engineering talent. It requires…
body: NASA’s Earth-observing satellite missions track dozens of features of a changing planet — aerosols, sea levels, land cover, cloud cover — over years and decades. Sustaining that record for the scientific and operational communities who depend on it requires more than engineering talent. It requires planning for an uncertain future: anticipating where a mission delay or on-orbit event might create a gap in the data those communities rely on. Lindsey Jacobson’s work helps NASA anticipate those disruptions before they happen and gives senior leaders options for managing them. title: Fan survey sends Google a pretty blunt message about the Pixel 12

body: Like it or not, Google has made AI a huge part of the Pixel experience, and that’s only become more obvious with the Pixel 11 series. Gemini Intelligence and other smart features were a major focus of this year’s launch — so much so that you’d assume this was what all the fans were screaming out for. It’s always quite tricky to know how true that is, so we were curious about where you think Google needs to go next with the Pixel 12. We recently asked our readers exactly that. My colleague Robert Trigg certainly has his own ideas about this direction, and made them abundantly clear in a recent article . His argument in a nutshell is that the Pixel 11 shows Google is approaching something of a hardware breaking point. He wasn’t unhappy with Google’s AI work, but pointed out that rival flagships are pushing ahead in fundamental areas such as battery capacity, charging speeds, camera hardware, and raw performance, while Pixels haven’t kept pace. With the Pixel 12 next to face that challenge, we asked you via a poll in the article whether Google should prioritize better hardware, even smarter AI, both, or simply more competitive prices.

title: Google expands Gemini’s interactive models to even more users
summary: Google brings Gemini's dynamic 3D models and simulations to Workspace.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Earlier this year, Google gave Gemini the ability to generate interactive simulations and models. This feature is now rolling out to all Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and users who meet the minimum age requirements. The update is available now in the Gemini app. If you’re having trouble understanding a complicated subject, sometimes visualization can do the trick. However, while an image can be helpful, having a visual model that you can actually interact with is even better. As Gemini is a tool that’s commonly used to help people understand complex concepts, it’s only natural that Gemini is gaining the ability to generate simulations and models. If this sounds familiar, it’s because Google announced the same feature back in April. However, Google says it is now rolling the feature out for Workspace users. This includes Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and users who meet the minimum age requirements.

title: One UI 9 Beta 6 finally lets you disable accidental AI Select triggers

Samsung is addressing one of the more frustrating gesture conflicts introduced on its recent flagships.
